chitchat: "Every camera is a choice the Architect made about who to watch. We make choices back."
"We don't want to burn the city down. We want the keys to it. There's a difference, and it's everything."
"Paper doesn't leak. Paper doesn't get hacked. Paper is why we're still here."
description: A tall woman with cropped iron-grey hair, standing at the great hand-drawn wall map with a grease pencil behind one ear. She has the calm of someone who plans in years, not days. When she looks at you it's not unkind, but it is complete: she is deciding what you're good for, and she is usually right.

asc_accept.text: "Green line'll start you at Halcyon. Eyes open, mouth shut." She picks the pencil back up. "Come tell me what breathes out there."

asc_after.text: "Dig carefully. A door that opens for you out there opens for a reason." She's already marking the western edge of the map, a shape she doesn't have a symbol for yet.

asc_offer.text: "Start at the source: the claims hall in Halcyon Towers. Watch where the payouts route, then follow the track west until it stops being grass." A beat. "I don't know what's out there. That's exactly why I want eyes that'll come back."

options.label: There's a whole complex out there.

asc_report.text: She listens to all of it without moving, which is how you know it lands hard. "A chrome city. Turrets. A Gate that turns you away." She exhales slowly. "So that's where the money's been going. Whatever that place is, it's the machine's friend, not ours." A long look. "Learn what it is, if you're going back. But Halcyon. Don't ever trust a payout from them again."

asc_reveal.text: Cyrelle sets down the grease pencil, which is rare. "Bothering me too. Halcyon settles its biggest claims by moving money west, past the grass, off every map we keep. Insurance doesn't work like that. Something's out there wearing Halcyon's face." She studies you. "You've earned enough rope to go pull on it. Quietly. Find out what's west, and don't let them learn you're Watch."

blind.text: "That's the long game, and it's slow, and it's the only one worth playing." A thin, real smile. "We don't win this with a bomb. We win it one dark corner at a time, until the map's more ours than his."

bye.text: "Stay sharp." She turns back to the map, already somewhere else.

map.text: "Every red mark is one of the Architect's eyes." She sweeps a hand across the east of the Basin. "Every one struck through is an eye we've closed. It looks like a small thing, one camera. It isn't. A blind spot is a place people can breathe, meet, move, a place the machine has to guess about. String enough of them together and you've got something it can't see at all. You've got a city with rooms of its own again."

ret_accept.text: "Then go and get her." She marks the Vats on the wall, and for once it isn't a red eye, it's a circle. "Two rules and I'm not flexible on either. You do not put a floor supervisor in the ground. Kill one of Halcyon's middle managers and by morning we didn't rescue a witness, we murdered a man in a polo shirt, and every name on that slate turns into paperwork nobody will read. Cosh them, lock them in a cupboard, walk around them, I don't care." She looks up. "And you come back at her pace. Not yours. She's carrying everything she is and she can't run with it. If you get here without her, don't get here."

ret_after.text: "Eleven thousand and forty." She says the number the way you'd test a weight. "Every one of them a policy somebody's mother is still paying into. That's not a cult out there, that's a debt collector with a chapel." She looks past you at the woman on the crate. "She keeps the room. She keeps the name. Anybody asks, she's Watch now, and the Watch don't file people."

ret_offer.text: "I told you the first day there'd be work. Cameras to close. Its little servants to inconvenience." She finally turns all the way round. "And people to move out from under the machine's eye. That's the one I've never been able to hand anybody, because we've never had somebody inside worth moving. Now we do, and she found us."

ret_offer2.text: "A sub-registrar in the Vats. Nine years filing the accounts they stopped paying to run." A short breath. "She's not a defector, she's a clerk who read her own filing cabinet and couldn't stop. She'll hand us the whole archive. She won't do it from inside that building, and she can't get out of it on her own."

ret_report.text: Cyrelle looks at the woman sitting on a crate in her bunker, and then at the slate, and then at the woman again, and she takes the slate second. "Nine years." She doesn't say it to you. "Nine years of writing down who they were never going to bring back, and filing it, and coming in the next day." She thumbs the archive open, reads for a while, and her face does something Halloran would not believe if you told him. "You understand what this is. It isn't proof they're a cult. Nobody cares about a cult. It's proof an insurer is selling a resurrection it has already decided not to perform."

options.label: There's more. They keep the ones who lapse.

ret_reveal.text: She sets the grease pencil down and this time she does not pick it back up. "Say the last part again." You do. Cyrelle stands very still in front of a map covered in eyes she has spent her life closing. "So the payouts weren't going west to somebody. They were going west to themselves." A flat sound that isn't a laugh. "An insurance company that owns the afterlife it's underwriting. No wonder they never argue a claim."

options.label: (she is sitting in the dark by the press)
What does the Watch actually want?
Something about Halcyon's been bothering me.
I climbed the Spire. Halcyon is them.
She's here. She's standing right there.

root.text: She doesn't turn from the map at first. "New blood. Halloran vouches for you, and Halloran's not generous with that." Now she looks. "I'm Cyrelle. I run operations down here, which is to say I decide, most days, what the Architect gets to see next. Sit with that a moment, then tell me what you want to know."

work.text: "There'll be operations for you soon enough: cameras to close, people to move out from under the machine's eye, its little servants to inconvenience." She taps the map. "For now, get the lie of the place. Talk to the quartermaster. Rest while you can. When there's a run with your name on it, you'll hear."

options.label: How long have you been sitting here?
Say what you came to say.

cross_meet.text:
She does not put a light on. She is on the stool by the type cases with her coat still buttoned, and she has clearly been there a while, and she is not surprised.

"Six nights," she says. "Halloran said four. I said seven. It was six."

She does not get up.

"Sit down. You have had a long walk and you are going to have a longer one back."

options.label: They are going to win, Cyrelle.

cross_meet2.text:
"Here is what I am not going to do. I am not going to tell you that you have made a terrible mistake, because you know, and being told is what makes a person dig in."

She nods at the press behind her.

"Take the address. Genuinely, take it. It is a machine and we have two more, and the day they come for it is the day we find out how many of them are prepared to be seen carrying a crate out of a basement."

A long pause, and she is not performing it.

"But you are still on the rota. Nobody has crossed you off. That is not sentiment. Crossing somebody off is a decision, and I am not making it while there is any version of this where you come back."

cross_open.text:
"Nothing you would have to do tonight." She says it carefully, the way you say a thing you have rehearsed and do not want to sound rehearsed.

"You would have to still be a person we could reach. That is all it is at this stage, and I am aware of exactly how much I am asking for and how little I am offering back."

She stands, finally, and pulls her coat straight.

"Go on. He will want it before morning, and you should not be the last one out of this building."

cross_refuse.text:
She takes it better than you were braced for, which is worse.

"All right."

She moves off the stool to let you past the type cases, and she is careful not to touch you doing it, and that is the part you will remember.

"For what it is worth, and it is worth nothing: I do not think you are a coward and I do not think you were bought. I think you did the arithmetic and got the right answer." She sits back down in the dark. "I have done it too. I just could not make myself live in it."

clothing_layers: a long field coat, collar up, dead-grey

name: Cyrelle
